posts.alt: Coronado coastal craftsman cottage side yard at dusk with a bronze fire-and-water bowl set on a ring of travertine steppers in artificial turf, olive trees in terracotta pots, low boxwood hedging, path lighting and tall palms against a warm sky
posts.hook: Not every backyard needs a party. Some just need one quiet corner that does everything.
posts.caption:
The whole point of this space is a single object — a bowl that runs fire and water at once.

It gives you the two things people actually come outside for. The flame for warmth and somewhere to rest your eyes after dark; the water for the sound that pulls the street noise out of a Coronado lot. Set it on a ring of travertine steppers in soft turf, light the olives from below, and a narrow side yard stops being a leftover strip and becomes the calmest seat on the property.

No pergola, no kitchen, no acreage required. One considered element, placed correctly, is the whole design.

The selections:
• bronze fire-and-water bowl (Bobe)
• silver travertine steppers
• SYNLawn artificial turf
• olive trees in terracotta
• FX Luminaire path & uplighting

posts.alt: North Park craftsman bungalow courtyard at dusk with a steel pergola and café string lights over a built-in ipe bench, a linear concrete fire feature, a living wall of ferns and succulents, a sphere water bowl and large-format porcelain pavers with a turf strip
posts.hook: A small yard isn't a compromise. It's a tighter brief.
posts.caption:
North Park lots don't give you room to waste — which is exactly why they reward good design.

Every element here is pulling more than one job. The pergola defines a room without a wall and carries the lighting. The bench is seating and it hides the mechanicals. The living wall does the work a big planting bed would, in four inches of depth. The linear fire feature anchors the space without eating the floor. Nothing is decorative-only, so a courtyard you can cross in six steps still feels like a full outdoor room.

On a compact lot the materials have to earn their place up close, because you see everything from three feet away. So we spend the budget on the surfaces and the details, not the square footage.

The selections:
• steel pergola with café string lighting
• large-format porcelain pavers
• linear concrete fire feature
• built-in ipe bench
• living wall + sphere water bowl

posts.style: Craft & Process · The Engineering Under the Fire
posts.alt: Macro close-up of polished brass Warming Trends CrossFire burners running clean flames over black lava rock inside a stone-capped fire pit, with an olive tree and estate backyard soft-focus behind at golden hour
posts.hook: This brass part is the difference between a fire that looks alive and one that looks like a stovetop.
posts.caption:
The best thing in a fire pit is the part you never see once it's finished.

Most pits run a simple steel ring — even ports, even gas, a flat blue row of flame. This is a Warming Trends CrossFire brass burner, and it works differently: it pulls in air as the gas moves through it, so it burns taller, more yellow, and with the flicker of real wood on far less fuel. Brass is here because it won't rust in a fire-and-weather cycle the way steel does, which is what keeps that flame pattern looking right in year five.

That's the whole SDLR argument in one component. The thing that lasts and the thing that looks good are usually the same decision, made early, out of sight.

The selections:
• Warming Trends CrossFire brass burner
• black lava rock media
• stone-capped fire pit surround
• concealed gas ignition

Want the fire that actually looks like fire? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Lifestyle · The Family Yard After Dark
posts.alt: Bonita Spanish-style two-story home at dusk with a paver patio, a round stucco gas fire pit with a stone-capped curved seat wall, chaise lounges, a rectangular turf lawn, citrus and bougainvillea, and café string lights overhead
posts.hook: The yard earns its keep after the sun goes down.
posts.caption:
A Bonita backyard built for the part of the day the whole family is actually home.

The curved seat wall does the quiet work — it holds the grade, wraps the fire, and seats a dozen people without a single chair to drag out. The turf panel keeps a soft, always-green run for the kids next to a hard patio that takes the furniture and the foot traffic. String lights bring the ceiling down to a human height once it's dark, so a big open yard suddenly feels like a room.

One fire, one lawn, one patio — but zoned so the adults can sit while the kids still have somewhere to be. That's the difference between a yard you look at and a yard you're all standing in at eight on a Tuesday.

The selections:
• Belgard paver patio
• round gas fire pit with stone-capped seat wall
• SYNLawn turf lawn
• café string lighting
• citrus, bougainvillea & low hedging

posts.style: Trust & Difference · One Contract, One Firm
posts.alt: Santaluz estate courtyard at golden hour with a tall stacked-stone outdoor fireplace, a large ivory linen sectional wrapping a square stone fire pit, olive trees, travertine paving and rolling golden hills behind a Spanish tile-roof home
posts.hook: A yard like this fails in the seams — where one trade hands off to the next.
posts.caption:
The stone mason, the gas fitter, the electrician, the paver crew, the framer for that fireplace — a space like this is five or six trades meeting in the same twenty feet.

When a homeowner hires those trades separately, they become the general contractor by accident. They're the one refereeing whose base the pavers sit on, why the fire pit gas line wasn't roughed in before the patio went down, who owns the crack that showed up at the hearth. That's where these projects go sideways — not in any one trade, but in the gaps between them.

We carry all of it on one contract, under one Class B license (CSLB #1139785). One schedule, one number, one firm accountable for the seams. The homeowner gets to just live here.

One firm. One plan. One honest number. By design, not by dispatch. References available on request.

The selections:
• Eldorado Stone stacked-stone fireplace
• limestone-capped stone fire pit
• ivory travertine paving
• custom linen sectional seating
• olive trees & path lighting
